qs.q: A 45-year-old patient presents with a deep-seated soft tissue mass in the thigh. Microscopic examination reveals mature fat cells, but genetic testing is required to distinguish this benign lesion from a well-differentiated liposarcoma. Which specific genetic alteration confirms a diagnosis of well-differentiated liposarcoma?
o: Detection of the t(X;18) SS18‑SSX translocation in tumor cells
Detection of the t(17;22) MYH9‑USP6 gene fusion in tumor cells
Detection of the t(12;16) FUS‑DDIT3 gene fusion in tumor cells
Detection of MDM2 and CDK4 gene amplification in tumor cells
qs.e: Well-differentiated liposarcomas look almost identical to lipomas under the microscope, and the only definitive way to tell them apart is by detecting MDM2/CDK4 gene amplification. The t(12;16) FUS-DDIT3 fusion is instead characteristic of myxoid liposarcoma.
